reach.rationale: No experimental or preview APIs at all; every runtime API is long-stable. The only 'very new' item is the single resolve.tsconfigPaths config line, recently stabilized in Vite 8.

containment.rationale: There is essentially nothing experimental to contain; the lone recently-stable option is a one-liner in the build config, trivially swappable.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:6 — tsconfigPaths replaces a third-party plugin with a built-in, a net simplification

justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used; the app stays on boring, stable primitives and hand-rolls behavior where a flashier new API might have been tempting.

findings.issue: resolve.tsconfigPaths is a Vite 8-era option whose @experimental documentation tag was removed only in July 2026 (vitejs/vite commit 961643a); it is stable but young.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is; if minimization of churn matters, it could be dropped or replaced with explicit relative imports, but the built-in is preferable to the vite-tsconfig-paths plugin it obviates.

summary: The app uses exclusively long-stable Framework Mode APIs — route config, server loaders, meta, ErrorBoundary, useSearchParams — with zero unstable_/experimental_ identifiers, no future flags, no middleware/RSC/client loaders. It tracks the current stable majors (React Router 8.5.1, Vite 8.0.3), which is version currency, not experimental reach. The only newly-stabilized API is the single resolve.tsconfigPaths config line, contained and justified.
